content.text:
The cases:
- "Hello World" -> "hello-world"
- "Node.js: The Good Parts!" -> "nodejs-the-good-parts" — note "." removed joining "Node" and "js" with no hyphen. Only whitespace becomes hyphens.
- "  many   spaces  " -> "many-spaces"
- "Top 10 Tips" -> "top-10-tips"

So: lowercase, remove non-letter/digit/space, collapse whitespace to hyphen, trim hyphens.

Note "Node.js:" -> "nodejs" then space -> hyphen. So punctuation removed entirely (not replaced by hyphen).

Implementation: title.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9\s]/g, '').replace(/\s+/g, '-').replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '').

Wait — `\s` includes newlines, tabs. Fine. But what about underscores? Underscore is not letter/digit/space, so stripped. Acceptable.

Edge: after stripping, characters like "é" would be removed. Tests don't cover. Keep simple.

Trim leading/trailing hyphens — use .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, ''). Since whitespace collapsed, only one hyphen possible at each end, but harmless.

```js
export function slugify(title) {
  return title
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9\s]/g, '')
    .trim()
    .replace(/\s+/g, '-');
}
```
